title: Petitions and demonstrations
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:38Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Petitions and demonstrations
card: a written request to parliament, signed by many people, asking for a law to be made or changed. It shows how many people support the change.
a public gathering, such as a march or rally, held to show support for or opposition to a law or issue. It draws public and media attention to the issue.
Both are ways for people to take part in law reform without holding office. Parliament can see that an issue matters to the community.
Neither can force parliament to change the law. Members of parliament decide whether to act, and they may take public support into account.
draft.remember: A petition shows how many people want change. A demonstration shows the issue to the public and the media.

a.q: What is the main thing a petition shows parliament about a proposed law change?
opts: How many people support the change
How the change would work in practice
That the change must now be debated
That the courts have approved the change
a.why: A petition collects signatures, so its strength is showing the number of people who want change. It does not make parliament debate or pass anything, because members of parliament still decide whether to act.
a.clue: Think about what a long list of signatures counts.

b.q: Residents of a Ballarat suburb want a law changed to protect a local creek. They hold a rally in the main street and the evening news covers it. What is the main effect of the rally on law reform?
opts: It draws public and media attention to the issue
It shows the exact number of people who back it
It requires parliament to debate a bill on the creek
It changes the law through a court decision
b.why: A rally is a demonstration, and its main strength is drawing public and media attention to the issue. It does not count supporters the way a petition does, and it cannot require parliament to act because members of parliament decide.
b.clue: A rally gets seen. Does it get counted or does it compel?

a.best: How many people support the change

b.best: It draws public and media attention to the issue
